static_traits.name: Lin Qing
static_traits.family_status: Living with spouse and two children
static_traits.social_status: Relationship tension with children; spouse gives emotional support; other social situations Not mentioned
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness history; no prior psychotherapy or psychiatric visits
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to recall specific situations; negative emotions, Anxiety intertwined with guilt; skeptical about treatment effects but willing to try; obvious self-blame tendency; moderate cooperation

basic_info.main_problem: The client values family but firmly believes 'the children hate me'; this feeling of being disliked by the children has lasted about a year, accompanied by increasing conflict in family interactions, leading to feeling isolated and suffering within the family.
basic_info.core_demands: Because these feelings negatively affect family relationships and mental health, the client hopes for professional guidance to ease the belief and pain of 'being hated by the children', improving getting along and interacting with them.
growth_experiences: In the past year, contradictions and small conflicts with the children increased (e.g., children playing phones at family game nights, disrespectful attitudes leading to arguments). In multiple family interactions, the client gradually formed the belief 'children do not want to be with me, they hate me', experiencing isolation and pain at home; raising her voice during conflicts, then feeling strong guilt and self-blame afterwards, further deepening helplessness and failure.

A few months ago, the client spent a day with the children at a park; the children laughed and played, interaction was smooth, and the client experienced a long-lost happiness and connection, feeling that 'the family was like what I had expected again'. But such positive fragments are considered rare and easily overlooked.

core_beliefs: I am a failure as a mother
I am not loved/not worthy of being loved

special_situations.event: Family game night ending in argument, children heads-down on phones, showing disrespect
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If children are not engaged or respectful in family activities, I am just a failure as a mother, they must hate me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling family activity organization, repeatedly expressing love to prove being a good mother; raising voice in arguments to control the situation
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They do not want to be with me, they hate me; I am a failed parent

special_situations.event: In the past year, contradictions and small conflicts with the children increased
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If conflicts grow more frequent, it means our relationship is worsening overall, they have never liked me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent self-blame, trying even harder to please the child, attempting to avoid any detail that might trigger conflict
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They have never liked me, I will never do well

special_situations.event: Feeling strongly disliked and isolated inside during family gatherings or interactions with children
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel left out, it means they really do not care about me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Becomes tense in advance and maintains high vigilance to prevent conflict; tightens emotions or intervenes in a controlling way during interaction
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can feel they dislike me; next time there will be another argument

special_situations.event: Occasional good moments of interaction (e.g., laughter watching movies together)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Brief pleasures do not represent the true situation, good moments do not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring positive evidence, continuing to search for dissatisfaction signs to prove the 'being hated' judgment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is just good luck; it will break down soon

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be genuinely accepted and close by the children, seen as a 'good mother'
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected and hated, losing worth and belonging in intimate relationships
defense_goal: Maintains the relationship and a sense of control through self-blame and redoubled effort, avoiding facing the fear of being disliked
Maintains high vigilance and control to prevent worse conflict outcomes

object_relations.self_representation: A flawed, easily disliked failure as a mother
object_relations.object_representation: Cold, critical children who reject closeness

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When children are heads-down on phones or unresponsive during family activities
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other party is rejecting me and our relationship (they hate me)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Mainly blaming and accusing, raised tone, absolute wording (e.g., 'you simply do not care about me'), interrupting when the other interprets.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others invite her to see positive evidence or hold uncertainty
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The other is negating my feelings, the problem will not be understood or changed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing 'this is useless' and 'it has always been terrible' in a cold, firm tone, reducing detail, shortening answers.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When worrying about being totally rejected and losing connection after relationship tension
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Only if I act more enthusiastic and more 'perfect' will the relationship be safe
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Speaking with excessive enthusiasm and pleasing, frequently using 'should/must' phrasing (e.g., 'I should do better to make everyone happy'), ignoring one's own feelings and boundaries.

manifestations: Experiencing isolation and not being needed in the family, believing children hate oneself
Persistently in a state of vigilance and exhaustion before and after interactions, expecting conflict to arrive
Treats the few positive moments as coincidences, hard to internalize as stable relationship experiences
outcomes: Ongoing emotional distress and Self-denial (guilt, shame)
Parent-child interaction deteriorates, conflict escalates, family functioning impaired
Wavering and a hollow feeling about self-worth and the meaning of relationships

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Frequent self-blame ('it is all my fault/I did not do well enough')
Tense in interactions, cautious, excessively anticipating negative outcomes
Skeptical about efficacy and Self-denial at the start of sessions

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Uses the standard 'a good mother should make everyone happy' to demand of oneself
Constraining one's emotions and behaviors with 'should/must'

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Attributing inner feelings of not being loved/accepted to 'children hating me'
Infers others' negative intentions without evidence

exception_events.target_problem: During daily interactions with children or family gatherings, the client usually quickly interprets conflicts as being hated, then emotionally loses control, raises her voice, worsening interactions.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few months ago during a family outing at the park, everyone played and laughed together; the client felt connected and needed, interactions went smoothly, with no arguments or feeling excluded.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different situation (outdoor, the park's relaxed atmosphere) and shared concrete activities brought positive engagement; the client could focus more on connection than conflict signs in the moment, so this interaction deviated from the usual negative cycle.

exception_events.target_problem: When with family, the client often takes the child's coldness or distraction as evidence of dislike, ignoring the few positive interactions.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A moment of shared laughter and harmonious atmosphere occurred while watching a movie with the child; the client felt relaxed and close.
exception_events.reason: Cues: jointly focusing on the same relaxing activity and less interference with each other's needs make it easier for the client to notice positive cues and form positive experiences.

positive_force: Highly values family, willing to invest time and energy to maintain the parent-child relationship
Able to identify and discuss negative automatic thoughts, willing to try recording positive moments
Receiving emotional support and understanding from spouse
In specific situations (such as outdoors or shared activities), able to experience genuine intimacy and connection
negative_force: Stable negative cognitive biases (mind-reading, predicting the future, overgeneralization, negating the positive, personalization)
Self-worth overly dependent on others' (children's) immediate feedback, leading to external validation tendency
Irritable and raising the voice during conflicts, intense guilt afterward, forming a vicious cycle
Persistent high vigilance and defensive interpretation, ignores positive evidence, relationships become further strained

target_behavior.behavior: In interactions with the child, is highly vigilant, irritable, and raises one's voice
antecedent: Children distracted by phones during family activities
Small frictions/non-cooperation at family gatherings or game nights
Tense state anticipating the next argument coming
target_behavior.core_reason: Based on the core belief 'I am a failure as a mother/children hate me' and catastrophic interpretation, trying to avoid the Fear of being rejected by controlling situations
target_behavior.function: Briefly gaining the illusion of control and respect, temporarily easing the Anxiety of being rejected
target_behavior.consequence: Escalating parent-child conflict, worsening relationship estrangement; the client afterwards develops strong guilt and self-blame, further reinforcing the negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated self-blame and negating positive evidence (persistent 'they hate me/I do not do well' automatic thoughts)
antecedent: Recalling interaction details after a conflict
When noticing negative cues before or after family interactions
target_behavior.core_reason: Inner failure and unloved core beliefs seeking self-verification, avoiding the discomfort of facing 'uncertainty'
target_behavior.function: Maintaining a certain interpretive framework to reduce Anxiety from uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, impaired attention, affected daily chores and role functioning; ignoring positive interactions, further solidifying negative beliefs
